title: GOATEST BAND (GT-Band)
subtitle: Modular Wearable Health Monitoring & Emergency Support System
shortDescription: GOATEST BAND (GT-Band) is a modular wearable health technology platform designed to provide personalized physiological monitoring, multi-location sensing, activity-aware insights, emergency support, and mobile connectivity through a reconfigurable wearable system.
fullDescription: GOATEST BAND, abbreviated as GT-Band, is a wearable health technology project developed as an alternative to conventional fixed-form smart wearables that primarily focus on wrist-based fitness measurements. The system combines embedded electronics, physiological sensors, wireless communication, local data storage, a companion application, and intelligent health-analysis software within a modular wearable platform. Its detachable sensing concept allows the platform to be adapted for different body locations and monitoring requirements while maintaining a common electronic and software ecosystem. The project includes a primary wearable unit, detachable sensing hardware, expandable module concepts, embedded firmware, mobile application integration, emergency communication capabilities, and personalized health assessment. The engineering prototype has been developed using development-grade electronics and is intended as a foundation for future miniaturization, validation, industrial hardware development, and product engineering.
problemStatement: Conventional smart bands and wearable devices generally use a fixed form factor and concentrate on a limited set of measurements from a single body location. This can make it difficult to adapt the same device for different sensing locations, personalized monitoring requirements, emergency situations, and future sensor expansion. Users may also need separate devices when monitoring requirements change. GT-Band addresses this product-level gap by combining a reconfigurable wearable form, expandable sensing, personalized health references, longitudinal records, and connected software within one platform.
solution: GT-Band provides a reusable wearable platform that can be configured for different physiological monitoring needs through its main wearable unit and detachable sensing modules. The system combines sensors, embedded processing, wireless communication, local storage, and a companion application to collect and present health-related information in a structured manner. Instead of depending only on generic reference ranges, the platform is designed to build a personalized reference for each user and use it to provide more relevant comparisons over time. The application can present measurements, historical changes, health summaries, alerts, guidance, and caregiver-oriented information. Emergency support is also incorporated as part of the overall product ecosystem.
architecture: Primary GT-Band wearable unit designed to house core processing, communication, power, storage, and user-interface electronics.
Detachable sensing module designed for repositionable physiological monitoring across selected body locations.
Expandable band architecture supporting future sensing modules and application-specific configurations.
ESP32-based embedded control platform for sensor acquisition, device management, communication, and wearable functions.
ESP32-C3 based detachable sensing node for modular wireless sensing and data exchange.
Multi-modal sensing support covering ECG, PPG/SpO2, motion, environmental and positioning-related information.
Personalized health reference system for comparing an individual's observations with their own historical physiological patterns.
Signal-quality and placement-aware acquisition approach to improve the reliability of wearable measurements.
Multi-parameter health assessment combining physiological observations with activity and environmental context.
Longitudinal health records organized across individual tests and longer-term time periods for observing changes.
Integrated emergency-support architecture with communication, location awareness, user interaction, and future caregiver connectivity.
Local storage capability using MicroSD technology to support data continuity when network connectivity is unavailable.
BLE communication for wearable-to-application connectivity with GSM support for wider-area communication requirements.
Modular embedded firmware developed using PlatformIO and VS Code to support continued hardware and software expansion.
innovation: Reconfigurable wearable concept that can support more than one sensing location instead of being restricted to a single fixed form factor.
Detachable sensing approach that allows the same primary wearable platform to support different monitoring configurations.
Personalized health referencing designed to make health information more relevant to the individual rather than relying only on generic population ranges.
Placement and signal-quality awareness designed to help obtain more usable wearable measurements.
Combination of physiological, motion, environmental, and contextual information for richer health and wellness insights.
Longitudinal health view that helps users observe changes across repeated assessments instead of relying only on isolated readings.
Integrated emergency-support capability within the same wearable ecosystem rather than requiring a completely separate emergency device.
Expandable hardware and software architecture that can accommodate additional sensors, modules, and future applications.
Unified wearable and mobile ecosystem combining embedded hardware, wireless communication, data storage, visualization, and intelligent assistance.
Product-oriented alternative to maintaining multiple dedicated wearable devices for different monitoring requirements.
futureWork: Develop a custom compact PCB and transition from development boards to production-oriented electronics.
Further reduce wearable size and weight through miniaturized components, optimized enclosure design, and flexible electronics.
Evaluate higher-grade physiological sensors and improve measurement consistency through controlled validation.
Expand the sensing platform with additional physiological and activity-related sensors where technically and clinically appropriate.
Improve wireless synchronization and secure cloud connectivity for optional remote health-data access.
Develop larger and more diverse datasets for improved personalized analytics and longitudinal pattern recognition.
Conduct comparative testing against established reference instruments and appropriate laboratory or clinical measurement methods.
Develop refined user interfaces for individuals, caregivers, and future professional monitoring workflows.
Strengthen emergency communication and location-support capabilities for different usage scenarios.
Progress the platform toward industrial design, regulatory assessment, manufacturing feasibility, and eventual commercialization.

milestones.title: Concept & Research
milestones.description: Established the initial wearable health-monitoring concept, studied existing wearable technologies, explored sensing requirements, and developed the early product architecture.

milestones.title: System Architecture
milestones.description: Developed the modular hardware concept, embedded architecture, communication structure, sensing configuration, and supporting software ecosystem.

milestones.title: Prototype Development
milestones.description: Built the initial working wearable platform using ESP32-based electronics, physiological sensors, communication modules, display hardware, and supporting embedded components.

milestones.title: Firmware & Application Integration
milestones.description: Expanded the embedded firmware, wireless communication, sensor acquisition, local storage, and application-side data workflow to create an integrated wearable system.

milestones.title: Patent & Engineering Documentation
milestones.description: Developed engineering documentation, system drawings, product architecture, technical workflows, and supporting patent documentation for the wearable platform.

milestones.title: Working Engineering Prototype
milestones.description: Reached a functional engineering prototype demonstrating modular wearable operation, physiological sensing, wireless connectivity, local data handling, application integration, and emergency-support concepts.

milestones.title: Product & Research Development
milestones.description: Continued development toward a more compact product architecture while advancing research documentation, software analytics, application capabilities, and future industrialization planning.
